_: Foundry's shelf. Each app here with a "dir" is built, signed with the release key and published by .github/workflows/android.yml whenever its folder changes. An app with a "prebuilt" APK instead is built in its own private repo and dropped in android/prebuilt; it is re-signed with the release key and published the same way (SayTap: mentifaber/Big-Button). Foundry reads each build's details (version, size, checksum, what changed) from its release, so editing words here never forces an update. Each app with a "twa" path is one of the site's web apps, built from the shared template in android/webapp with its own id, name, colour and logo. "status": "soon" lists an app as Coming soon (a demo, simulator, sample or site page): never offered for install, and not built; "private" means it works but needs an invite or a password, and it stays installable. To add an app: put its Gradle project in android/<name>, give it an entry here, push.

apps.name: AutoFaber
apps.tagline: A mind with a name, and every model on call
apps.description:
AutoFaber remembers you, talks with you out loud and calls on every AI model it can reach: one at a time in the Studio, as a council that merges the best drafts, or as a swarm that builds whole projects you can run. Live web search with sources, vision, pictures, weather, quotes for any stock or coin, and phone alerts from Vigil.

On Android it runs full screen in Chrome's own engine, so voice, the microphone, sign-in, uploads and notifications work just as they do on the web.

apps.name: MentiPlayer
apps.tagline: Films, TV, music, radio and podcasts in one player
apps.description:
One player for films, classic TV, live TV, music from every artist, radio, audiobooks and podcasts, from open sources and the ones their owners stream for free: the Internet Archive, the Library of Congress, NASA, YouTube, SomaFM, Mixcloud and more. Search everything at once, queue songs, save what you like, and pick up where you left off.

Safe mode is on unless you turn it off, so it stays family-friendly. On Android it runs full screen in Chrome's own engine, with background playback just like the web.

apps.name: SayTap
apps.tagline: Four giant buttons you can tap, or just say
apps.description:
Four giant buttons, Phone, Search, Talk and YouTube, that you can tap or just say out loud: say “call Mom” or “YouTube cat videos” and it happens. Made for low vision, shaky hands, and anyone who'd rather talk than type.

Calls open the dialer so you still press call yourself, searches and videos open in the browser or the YouTube app, and Talk opens AutoFaber's voice. Speech recognition and the spoken replies use the phone's own voice services. It's private: nothing is collected.

apps.name: Thoughtform
apps.tagline: A shooter fought inside a mind under siege
apps.description:
A first-person shooter set inside a mind under siege, built from nothing but maths: a hand-written raymarched world and live-synthesized sound, with no engine, models, textures or samples. Eleven kinds of intrusive thought, each with its own attack; the Critic every fifth wave; four regions that sink deeper the longer you last, with lightning and gravity wells underfoot; and an Insight to choose after every wave, from double jump to Undertow.

On Android it runs full screen in Chrome's own engine with touch controls, and your progress, Codex and leaderboard come with it.
features: Eleven kinds of thought, each with its own attack
Insights that change how you play

apps.name: Tether
apps.tagline: One-finger rope swinging over lava
apps.description: A one-finger rope-swinging game, open to everyone: real rope physics over lava through ten biomes with their own weather and soundtracks. Saws, drones, rockets, fire spouts, speed lasers and world-flipping rings; ten stackable power-ups; eleven modes including co-op, racing, time trial and the daily course; a ghost of your best run, and an online lobby where you can challenge anyone playing to a live head-to-head race.

apps.name: Sideways
apps.tagline: Drift, and the soundtrack plays itself
apps.description: A drifting game Claude made for Anders where the soundtrack is played by how you drive: get sideways and an arpeggio comes in, hold it and the bass and lead follow, every orb is a note on the beat. Four tracks, one boxy wagon.

apps.name: Graveyard Shift
apps.tagline: Keep the satellites talking until dawn
apps.description: A night-shift orbit game Claude designed and built for Anders with no input from him: put relay satellites into real orbits, route signals across the network, and keep the stations talking until dawn.

apps.name: Root Cause
apps.tagline: The pager's going off: find the first domino
apps.description: An on-call detective game Claude made for Anders, unprompted: the pager goes off, the logs are full of red herrings, and you run real checks to find the first domino. Ten incidents, a rubber duck, an endless rotation.

apps.name: Watch Your Grass
apps.tagline: Defend a six-by-six lawn from its visitors
apps.description: Arena defense on a 6×6 lawn: ten plant and terrain types, six kinds of visitor, drawn up on paper before a line of code and now playable in the browser.

apps.name: Barycenter
apps.tagline: A private, encrypted universe for two
apps.description: A private universe for two: messages, voice notes, touch and presence, encrypted end to end and kept on your own devices. Invite-only.

apps.name: Pilotfish
apps.tagline: A shared list and a quiet line for two
apps.description: A shared list and a quiet signal line for two: what to grab, how you feel, what you need. Push alerts, photos, offline.

apps.name: NULLSPACE
apps.tagline: Encrypted comms over the internet and mesh radio
apps.description: An encrypted comms deck that talks over the internet and over LoRa mesh radio (Meshtastic and MeshCore). No account, no phone number: pick a handle, tune a frequency, transmit.

apps.name: Hopline
apps.tagline: Chat across a LoRa mesh, no towers needed
apps.description: A front-end for a Meshtastic LoRa mesh. Connect your radio over USB or Bluetooth and message the mesh, see every node, how many hops away it is and how strong it sounds: every radio is a relay and no tower sits in the middle. No radio? A simulated valley of radios shows how the mesh floods messages.

apps.name: Skipline
apps.tagline: HF radio chat with the internet switched off
apps.description: HF radio chat that works with the internet switched off — a browser VARA client verified to make zero external calls. Air-gapped by design.

apps.name: Nobody
apps.tagline: A terse voice assistant that never goes silent
apps.description:
Nobody, in the browser: a terse voice assistant with a fluid orb you tap to talk to. It answers out loud, reads the time, your battery and where you are, sets timers, opens and shares things, and when the voice drops it degrades to text instead of going silent.

On Android it runs full screen in Chrome's own engine, with the microphone and speech working just as they do on the web.

apps.name: Phone MCP
apps.tagline: Watch a model drive an Android phone
apps.description: A model on the internet driving a real Android phone — MCP over a Cloudflare tunnel, down a USB cable, into ADB. Four links, every one accounted for.

apps.name: Cartograph
apps.tagline: A 3D atlas from the planets to the first galaxies
apps.description: A 3D atlas from the planets to the first galaxies: 140+ objects at their real positions across ten views, each cited to the instrument that measured it, plus live satellites around Earth.

apps.name: Overhead
apps.tagline: Live satellites, and every pass over you
apps.description: Live satellite tracking from CelesTrak element sets, propagated with SGP4 in your browser: ground tracks, the day-night line, and every pass over you, with the ones you can see by eye marked.

apps.name: Bodywake
apps.tagline: See a body's shadow on ambient WiFi
apps.description: Detects a person walking through a house from the shadow their body casts on ambient WiFi. No camera, no wearable, no app on their phone.

apps.name: Moodfield
apps.tagline: Simulations of emotional state, honestly told
apps.description: Simulations of emotional state and a consciousness protocol — with a straight account of what the runs do not prove.

apps.name: Synodic
apps.tagline: Two dates, two moons, one score
apps.description: Any two dates placed on the synodic cycle, both moons drawn and overlaid, the gap between them read as a compatibility score.

apps.name: Omnilogos
apps.tagline: 933,573 verses in one navigable graph
apps.description: 933,573 verses across thirty translations, wired into one navigable graph — the most comprehensive concordance attempted, fully local.

apps.name: Unlit
apps.tagline: Twenty-eight wars, tiered by scale
apps.description: Twenty-eight active conflicts, tiered by scale rather than by how much coverage they get. Data as of June 2026.

apps.name: Per Capita
apps.tagline: US city crime, ranked by rate, not counts
apps.description: Forty-three US cities, four crime categories, FBI data projected to 2025 — ranked by rate per 100,000, not raw counts, in one file you can email to anyone.

apps.name: Ballast
apps.tagline: Every bill on a calendar, and what's safe to spend
apps.description: Every bill on a real calendar, ninety days projected forward, and one honest number: what's safe to spend today. Local-first — the numbers never leave the browser.

apps.name: Duely
apps.tagline: Chase overdue invoices, politely
apps.description: Overdue invoices, chased politely: three dated reminders, friendly to firm, checked against hard legal guardrails and sent from your own mail app. You pay nothing unless your client does.

apps.name: CryptoVault
apps.tagline: Encryption you can read to the bottom of
apps.description: Encryption you can read to the bottom of: RSA-4096 and AES-256-GCM in one HTML file, with identities, contacts, signatures and files. No server, no dependency, and no network call allowed.

apps.name: DocCrawler
apps.tagline: Your documents, read, indexed and asked
apps.description: A document library that lives in your browser: drop in PDFs, Word files, notes and photos of paper, and DocCrawler reads them (OCR included), indexes and tags everything for full-text search, and lets you ask the Librarian questions answered from your own files, with citations. Nothing leaves the device.

apps.name: Eightysixty
apps.tagline: A web remote for your Roku TV
apps.description: A self-hosted web remote for Roku TVs — auto-discovery, every button, inputs, a channel grid and a real keyboard, talking straight to the TV over the local network. No Roku account, no cloud.

apps.name: Worm Eater
apps.tagline: An ingredient scanner that admits what it doesn't know
apps.description: An ingredient scanner for food, cosmetics and personal care that says "I don't know" instead of quietly scoring the unknowns as safe. Five open databases.

apps.name: Sleep Compression
apps.tagline: Sleep restriction, tracked night by night
apps.description: A sleep-restriction protocol turned tracker — log nights, get sleep efficiency, and know exactly when to widen the window. The Obsidian vault is included.

apps.name: Mechanic's Arsenal
apps.tagline: Machines you can take apart in the browser
apps.description: Machines you can take apart in the browser — a 2008 Volvo XC70 with 126 cataloged parts, and a FANUC LR Mate robot arm you can jog, solve and run, every spec cited to the manual.

apps.name: Balloon
apps.tagline: Balloon a drawing for first-article inspection
apps.description: Ballooning an engineering drawing for first-article inspection — drag numbered callouts into place, load your own drawing, export the sheet.

apps.name: The Shop
apps.tagline: Program a lathe in G-code and watch it cut
apps.description: A lathe you program in G-code: write or load a program for a FANUC-style turning centre, run it a block at a time or all at once, and watch the tool cut the stock, with the cycle time, cutting path and every move it makes. Start from sample parts, or type your own.

apps.name: The Monstrosity
apps.tagline: A homelab opened up, layer by layer
apps.description: A bolted-together homelab, build log 001 — three machines on a private line, ten drives in one namespace, Traefik routing, and a tunnel as the only door.

apps.name: Sonic Veil
apps.tagline: Ten years of ambient and electronic music
apps.description: Composer since 2016 — ambient, experimental and electronic. 86 tracks, ten years of genre-bending, streaming on 150+ platforms.

apps.name: Foundry
apps.tagline: Every Mentifaber app, installed and kept up to date
apps.description:
The home of Mentifaber's Android apps. Install any of them in a tap, open and remove them, and let Foundry keep them current: it checks for new versions twice a day, and on Android 12 and later it installs updates to the apps it installed without asking each time.

Every download is checked before it is installed. Its checksum must match the catalog, its package name must be the app's, and it must be signed with the same key as Foundry itself, so nothing else can slip in.
features: Every APK checked against Mentifaber's signature
